key_idea: Minimize the functional τ = d[X1;X2] + η(d[X1^0;X1] + d[X2^0;X2]) over all pairs of distributions. A minimizer must have zero entropic Ruzsa distance, because otherwise the fibring identity applied to sums and differences of independent copies, together with an entropic Balog–Szemerédi–Gowers step, would produce a pair with smaller τ. Zero distance then forces both variables to be uniform on a subgroup.
reason: The compactness/minimizer framing turns the whole PFR problem into one statement: zero distance at an extremizer. The fibring identity is a short, reusable, conceptual tool that explains where the decrease comes from. What holds it back from a book proof is the bookkeeping: the endgame needs permutation averaging, several entropy estimates, and tuned constants (η = 1/9), and these fix the final constant without being forced by the idea.
recognized: Gowers–Green–Manners–Tao, 'On a conjecture of Marton' (proof of the Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture over F_2^n with C=12)
